kicker: Most Wanted in a browser tab

scenes.headline: How Most Wanted got into a browser tab
scenes.sub: A 2005 racer, read from outside its login wall
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Nacelle! A fan project runs Need for Speed Most Wanted in Chrome, online. The game sits behind a login, so here is the outside.

scenes.text: It draws with WebGPU and streams its files from a CDN, but its game logic is being rebuilt one original behaviour at a time.
scenes.mark: one original behaviour at a time
scenes.say: The idea: it draws with WebGPU and pulls files from a download network, but its game logic is being rebuilt, one original behaviour at a time.

scenes.title: What sits on each side of the login

steps.say: Logged out, you get one page, a logo and two screenshots. No scripts, no WebAssembly.
Its one check: does this browser have WebGPU?
The game client loads only after login. I made no account.
Files come from a storage bucket on a fast download network. Careers live on their server.

scenes.title: Four ways into a browser tab
scenes.say: Four ways to put an old Windows game in a tab.

items.say: Recompile the studio's own source, as the GTA Five port did.
Rebuild source from the binary, then compile it.
Run the original program, translating as it goes. Slow, and hard to change.
Or write a new engine around the game's data.

left.title: If the original ran
items: Police already follow the road map
left.say: If the original code ran, police would already follow the road map, and speeding would already start at a hundred and thirty.

right.title: What the notes say
items: Fixed: now like the original game
Carbon's canyons and vinyls moved in
right.say: Instead the fixes say: now like the original game. And pieces of Carbon move in. That is code the team can edit.

scenes.title: A view the game never had

steps.say: New features land daily, like a cockpit view with hands on the wheel.
And a rear-view mirror, off on phones and in lite mode.

scenes.label: of the PC code matched by the public decompilation
scenes.note: nothing public links it to this site
scenes.say: The public decompilation of this game matches under fourteen percent of the PC code. Nothing links it to this site.

scenes.text: A changelog full of fixes that restore the original is evidence of rewritten code, not the shipped binary.
scenes.say: Remember: fixes that restore the original are evidence of rewritten code, not the shipped program.

recap: WebGPU renderer, files from a Cloudflare bucket
Original behaviours restored one by one
Engine code stays behind the login
